title: Philadelphia County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Philadelphia County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Pennsylvania
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Philadelphia County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Philadelphia County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Pennsylvania statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Philadelphia County recorder of deeds records Pennsylvania deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Philadelphia County

  • Department of Records records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Effective July 1, 2025 deed recording fee increased from $274.75 to $277.75; city realty transfer tax rate increased from 3.278% to 3.578%.

Recording and transfer tax

  • PA realty transfer tax is imposed at 1 percent on the value of real estate (including contracted-for improvements) transferred by deed, instrument, long-term lease or other writing; grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable. (72 P.S. 8102-C (per DOR page); 61 Pa. Code 91.111(a)-(b), 72 P.S. 8107-C authority; source)
  • 61 Pa. Code 91.111: state tax at 1% of value of realty; it is the joint and several legal duty of the parties to pay; the duty may be discharged as the parties agree without prejudice to the Commonwealth's rights. (61 Pa. Code 91.111 (authority 72 P.S. 8107-C); source)
  • State RTT is collected, often with an additional local realty transfer tax, by county Recorders of Deeds; Recorders remit the 1% to the Dept of Revenue; locals may share their RTT among school districts and municipalities. (DOR Realty Transfer Tax overview (no statute cite on page); source)
  • The 1% state realty transfer tax is generally due when a document transferring title is filed with the county Recorder of Deeds; payment is evidenced by a stamp or impression affixed to the document. (72 P.S. 8101-C et seq.; DOR RTT Q&A; source)
  • Recorders of Deeds and commissioners of records are agents for sale of RTT stamps; a statement of value (REV-183) in duplicate is filed with a document presented for recording or for tax stamps, specifying true full value and why the instrument is not taxable. (61 Pa. Code 91.114, 91.112; Form REV-183; source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Philadelphia County?
We buy Philadelphia County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • 2026 tax year rate not seen

How to sell a house in Philadelphia County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the Register of Wills paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Pennsylvania.

What a cash sale of a Philadelphia County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Philadelphia County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Pennsylvania disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Philadelphia County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Pennsylvania change, so confirm details with the official office or a Pennsylvania attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Philadelphia County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Philadelphia County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Philadelphia County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.

title: York County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
York County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Pennsylvania
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in York County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy York County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Pennsylvania statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The York County recorder of deeds records Pennsylvania deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in York County

  • York County Recorder of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recordings accepted by mail, in person, and e-recording.
  • Statement of Value required whenever consideration is not full market value; family transfer statement typed on deed if tax not paid; UPI required on all documents.
  • Payment by cash, business check or money order payable to Recorder of Deeds; overage under $10 not returned.

Recording and transfer tax

  • PA realty transfer tax is imposed at 1 percent on the value of real estate (including contracted-for improvements) transferred by deed, instrument, long-term lease or other writing; grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable. (72 P.S. 8102-C (per DOR page); 61 Pa. Code 91.111(a)-(b), 72 P.S. 8107-C authority; source)
  • 61 Pa. Code 91.111: state tax at 1% of value of realty; it is the joint and several legal duty of the parties to pay; the duty may be discharged as the parties agree without prejudice to the Commonwealth's rights. (61 Pa. Code 91.111 (authority 72 P.S. 8107-C); source)
  • State RTT is collected, often with an additional local realty transfer tax, by county Recorders of Deeds; Recorders remit the 1% to the Dept of Revenue; locals may share their RTT among school districts and municipalities. (DOR Realty Transfer Tax overview (no statute cite on page); source)
  • The 1% state realty transfer tax is generally due when a document transferring title is filed with the county Recorder of Deeds; payment is evidenced by a stamp or impression affixed to the document. (72 P.S. 8101-C et seq.; DOR RTT Q&A; source)
  • Recorders of Deeds and commissioners of records are agents for sale of RTT stamps; a statement of value (REV-183) in duplicate is filed with a document presented for recording or for tax stamps, specifying true full value and why the instrument is not taxable. (61 Pa. Code 91.114, 91.112; Form REV-183; source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in York County?
We buy York County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Indecomm e-recording vendor from search snippet only
  • Assessor facts from search snippets only

How to sell a house in York County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the Register of Wills paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Pennsylvania.

What a cash sale of a York County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in York County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Pennsylvania disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in York County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Pennsylvania change, so confirm details with the official office or a Pennsylvania attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in York County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

York County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in York County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Pennsylvania statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Cumberland County recorder of deeds records Pennsylvania deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Cumberland County

  • Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Deed and mortgage fee $104.75 first 4 pages (eff. Nov 17, 2025); $2/page over 4; $0.50/name over 4; Statement of Value $1.00; includes $20 UPI fee if required.
  • PA realty transfer tax 1% state, collected by county Recorders often with local tax.

Recording and transfer tax

  • PA realty transfer tax is imposed at 1 percent on the value of real estate (including contracted-for improvements) transferred by deed, instrument, long-term lease or other writing; grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable. (72 P.S. 8102-C (per DOR page); 61 Pa. Code 91.111(a)-(b), 72 P.S. 8107-C authority; source)
  • 61 Pa. Code 91.111: state tax at 1% of value of realty; it is the joint and several legal duty of the parties to pay; the duty may be discharged as the parties agree without prejudice to the Commonwealth's rights. (61 Pa. Code 91.111 (authority 72 P.S. 8107-C); source)
  • State RTT is collected, often with an additional local realty transfer tax, by county Recorders of Deeds; Recorders remit the 1% to the Dept of Revenue; locals may share their RTT among school districts and municipalities. (DOR Realty Transfer Tax overview (no statute cite on page); source)
  • The 1% state realty transfer tax is generally due when a document transferring title is filed with the county Recorder of Deeds; payment is evidenced by a stamp or impression affixed to the document. (72 P.S. 8101-C et seq.; DOR RTT Q&A; source)
  • Recorders of Deeds and commissioners of records are agents for sale of RTT stamps; a statement of value (REV-183) in duplicate is filed with a document presented for recording or for tax stamps, specifying true full value and why the instrument is not taxable. (61 Pa. Code 91.114, 91.112; Form REV-183; source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

What a cash sale of a Cumberland County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Cumberland County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.

  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Pennsylvania disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Cumberland County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Cumberland County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.

title: Wayne County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Wayne County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Pennsylvania
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Wayne County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Wayne County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Pennsylvania statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Wayne County recorder of deeds records Pennsylvania deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Wayne County

  • Wayne County Recorder of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

Recording and transfer tax

  • PA realty transfer tax is imposed at 1 percent on the value of real estate (including contracted-for improvements) transferred by deed, instrument, long-term lease or other writing; grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable. (72 P.S. 8102-C (per DOR page); 61 Pa. Code 91.111(a)-(b), 72 P.S. 8107-C authority; source)
  • 61 Pa. Code 91.111: state tax at 1% of value of realty; it is the joint and several legal duty of the parties to pay; the duty may be discharged as the parties agree without prejudice to the Commonwealth's rights. (61 Pa. Code 91.111 (authority 72 P.S. 8107-C); source)
  • State RTT is collected, often with an additional local realty transfer tax, by county Recorders of Deeds; Recorders remit the 1% to the Dept of Revenue; locals may share their RTT among school districts and municipalities. (DOR Realty Transfer Tax overview (no statute cite on page); source)
  • The 1% state realty transfer tax is generally due when a document transferring title is filed with the county Recorder of Deeds; payment is evidenced by a stamp or impression affixed to the document. (72 P.S. 8101-C et seq.; DOR RTT Q&A; source)
  • Recorders of Deeds and commissioners of records are agents for sale of RTT stamps; a statement of value (REV-183) in duplicate is filed with a document presented for recording or for tax stamps, specifying true full value and why the instrument is not taxable. (61 Pa. Code 91.114, 91.112; Form REV-183; source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Wayne County?
We buy Wayne County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How to sell a house in Wayne County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the Register of Wills paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Pennsylvania.

What a cash sale of a Wayne County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Wayne County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Pennsylvania disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Wayne County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Pennsylvania change, so confirm details with the official office or a Pennsylvania attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Wayne County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Wayne County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Wayne County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.

  • Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
